title: Hostile coverage: scheduler and activation authority boundaries
description:

HARD DEPENDENCY: task-9aca4b0524a648f1841237b40d4e345b (Security lane harness and declared-boundary roster) must be DONE — this slice consumes its harness and claims its `scheduler-activation` axis tag. Re-measure on disk before planning.

- apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ingress-contracts.ts:74,75,76 — ACTIVATION_INGRESS_LAYER, ACTIVATION_SLOT_LAYER, ACTIVATION_BUDGET_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/activation/foundation-activation-transition.ts:85 — FOUNDATION_ACTIVATION_BINDING_LAYER
- apps/daemon/src/work/work-kernel.ts:73 — WORK_LAYERS
- apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:36,37 — SCHEDULER_GRAPH_LAYER, RUNNER_WORKSPACE_LAYER
- packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-measurement.ts:32 — MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS
- packages/scheduler/src/convergence/breaker-contract.ts:17 — CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_LAYER
- packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-current-hold.ts:52 — EXPANSION_BINDING_LAYERS
- packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-receipt.ts:35 — EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_LAYERS
- packages/scheduler/src/fairness/fairness-contract.ts:30 — FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_LAYERS
- packages/scheduler/src/readiness/readiness-model.ts:47 — READINESS_LAYERS
- apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion-evidence.ts:42,43,44 — CORE_APPROVAL_LAYER, PROJECT_REDUCER_LAYER, DAEMON_INGRESS_LAYER

Deliverable: hostile schedules — a grant consumed twice, a slot claimed concurrently by two attempts, budget exhaustion presented as headroom, a stale readiness verdict replayed after the graph moved, an expansion receipt bound to a superseded revision, a fairness decision raced against a convergence breaker trip, and an activation whose binding no longer matches its transition — each pinning the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer.

TWO-SIDED BUDGET HAZARD: an unmeasured budget and a zero budget are different facts. A case that lets UNKNOWN usage be rendered as zero, or imputed from a sibling attempt, must fail; assert that explicitly rather than assuming the production surface already refuses.

NOT in scope: transport, integrity/codec, durable store, or runtime/provider boundaries; closing the completeness ratchet; anything under tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/scheduler-activation-boundaries.security.ts (plus at most one sibling file if the 400-line split applies).

Verification: `pnpm test:security` — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code.
definitionOfDone: Every constant in the scheduler-activation subset has at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case, with a positive case count asserted per constant so a boundary generating zero cases reddens.

Every refusal pins the exact stable reason code AND the answering layer; where ingress, slot and budget layers can all refuse the same activation, each fixture is valid at the earlier layers so the intended one provably answers.

A grant consumed twice and a slot claimed concurrently each yield exactly one admitted activation and one stable refusal — never two admissions, never two refusals — with the durable state read back to prove it.
An UNKNOWN usage measurement is never rendered as zero and never imputed across attempts; a case drives an unmeasured attempt and asserts the refusal rather than a zero-cost admission.
A mutation removing one grant-consumption or slot-exclusion check from a covered production boundary turns a NAMED test red, with the drill confirming the red lands on the intended assertion.
Each race case is BOUNDED and terminates; the test itself is bounded, because the failure mode guarded against is a hang and a hang reports no verdict.

`pnpm test:security` runs with its exit code captured separately and prints a count line strictly above the pre-task baseline; the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Consume the roster's `scheduler-activation` axis tag as the definitive subset; the roster owns the partition.

Fail closed: an unmeasured budget, an unresolved readiness verdict, or an unverifiable binding stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority. A zero cost and an unmeasured cost are different facts and must not collapse.
Assert against the production surface, never a test helper that reimplements a budget rule, a fairness ordering, or a readiness verdict.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec. Do not touch tests/fault/**.

implementationPlan.description:
ACTIVATION ADMISSION ARMS — ACTIVATION_INGRESS_LAYER, ACTIVATION_SLOT_LAYER, ACTIVATION_BUDGET_LAYER, ACTIVATION_LEDGER_LAYER, FOUNDATION_ACTIVATION_BINDING_LAYER, SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER, DOCUMENT_WORK_SERVICE_LAYERS.
HOSTILE INPUT: a grant presented twice; a grant whose binding names a different effect intent, wrapper identity or session than the committed activation; a slot claimed while another attempt holds it; an activation whose transition no longer matches its binding; a spawn request whose argv cannot be quoted; a document-work proposal for a subject the caller does not own.
THE EXCLUSIVITY ASSERTION, which is this group's substance: a grant consumed twice and a slot claimed concurrently must each yield EXACTLY ONE admitted activation and one stable refusal — never two admissions, never two refusals. Read the durable state back to prove it; a returned refusal is not evidence that nothing was written.
THE REPLAY-ECHO TRAP, measured and specific to `ACTIVATION_LEDGER_LAYER`: the store's replay identity does NOT cover the events array (activation-ledger-commit.ts:12-24). A replay answered with the caller's own record makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and pass forever. So the hostile replay case here must present a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT record under the same command key and assert the FIRST record's bytes come back, read from the durable aggregate. Without that, this boundary's coverage is vacuous no matter how many cases it has.
BUDGET IS TWO-SIDED: an unmeasured budget and a zero budget are different facts. Drive an attempt whose usage is UNKNOWN and assert the refusal rather than a zero-cost admission, and assert no value is imputed from a sibling attempt.
Every refusal through `assertRefusedWith` with code and layer, each layer from the boundary's own constant. Ingress, slot and budget can all answer one activation — build each fixture valid at the earlier layers and name the arranged layer in a comment.

implementationPlan.description:
EXPANSION, SUPERSESSION AND GRAPH ARMS — EXPANSION_APPROVAL_LAYERS, EXPANSION_HOLD_LAYERS, EXPANSION_PREPARATION_LAYERS, PLANNING_EXPANSION_LAYERS, EXPANSION_BINDING_LAYERS, EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_LAYERS, GRAPH_REVISION_LAYER, SUPERSESSION_KERNEL_LAYER, SUPERSESSION_DISPOSITION_LAYERS, GOAL_LAYER, SCHEDULER_GRAPH_LAYER, WORK_LAYERS.
HOSTILE INPUT: an expansion approval bound to a superseded graph revision; a preparation released after its hold expired; an expansion receipt whose evidence names a different revision; a supersession disposition presented for a node the kernel never superseded; a graph revision replayed after the graph moved; a goal closure witness for a different goal; a work claim whose lease no longer holds.
THE STALE-BINDING FAMILY IS THE POINT HERE. Every one of these boundaries guards "is this decision still bound to the thing it was made about?", so the AFTER arm carries most of the weight: present a decision that was valid, move the subject, present it again, and assert the exact refusal code and layer. A BEFORE-only suite would pass against an implementation with no binding recheck at all.
SUPERSESSION HAS TWO LAYERS IN SERIES — the core kernel (`SUPERSESSION_KERNEL_LAYER`) and the scheduler's disposition (`SUPERSESSION_DISPOSITION_LAYERS`). A fixture invalid at the kernel never reaches the disposition, so name the arranged layer per case; the same applies to expansion, where core approval/hold/preparation sit ahead of the scheduler's binding and evidence.
RACE: two conflicting approvals for one subject; a supersession racing a claim on the superseded node; an expansion hold racing its own expiry. Bound well below `MAX_BOUND_MS` (2**31-1, where `setTimeout` clamps to 1ms), assert per-side via `RaceOutcome` that exactly one is admitted or both refuse, and make each case pass whichever side wins — an order-dependent race is a flake whose usual fix pins the order and destroys the property.
implementationPlan.note:
EXPANSION/SUPERSESSION/GRAPH GROUP COMPLETE — 10 constants, 20 of the roster's 24 now covered. Suite: 91 cases, 86 pass; the 5 remaining failures are all step-4's four scheduler-decision constants plus the roster-set assertion.

EVERY EXPECTED CODE OR LAYER I INFERRED FROM READING THE SOURCE WAS WRONG SOMEWHERE, and running is what found it. Six corrections, all made against observed production output rather than against the vocabulary I had read:
- GRAPH_REVISION_LAYER and GOAL_LAYER refuse with `UNKNOWN_ERROR`, not `UNKNOWN_FAILURE`. The constructor is named `unknownFailure()`, which is where the wrong guess came from — the function name is not the code.
- SUPERSESSION_DISPOSITION_LAYERS refuses with `INPUT_INVALID` at layer `SCHEDULER_SUPERSESSION_SET`. I had written `SUPERSESSION_REQUEST_MALFORMED` at `REQUEST` — both halves wrong, and `REQUEST` is not even a member of that vocabulary.
- EXPANSION_EVIDENCE_LAYERS answers at `EVIDENCE`, not `INPUT`, despite `INPUT` being a declared member of its layer list. A plausible-looking member is not the one that answers.
- PLANNING_EXPANSION targets are spelled `HOLD_BINDING`, not `holdBinding`; the lowercase form fell through to `PLANNING_EXPANSION_TARGET_INVALID`, so the case would have asserted an unknown-target refusal while claiming to cover binding validation.

THE HOLD AFTER ARM IS THE ONE WORTH READING. Written as a stale-version case, it came back `EXPANSION_HOLD_INPUT_INVALID` — the parser mirrors a CLOSED key set (`CREATE_KEYS`, 16 fields with hex64 digests, a nested rationale whose truthClass must be AGENT_REPORTED, and full release-evidence and handoff sub-records), so my six-field command was rejected at the input layer and the concurrency check was never reached. That is exactly the layers-in-series defect this slice exists to catch, and it was in my own fixture. Now built valid to the full key set, so `EXPANSION_HOLD_STALE_VERSION` at `CONCURRENCY` is genuinely reached and the after arm tests version currency rather than input parsing.

AFTER ARMS DRIVE A MOVED SUBJECT, not just a second malformed input: an approval whose claim names a preparation since re-prepared; a hold command replayed at a version the state has left behind; a create command replayed against an existing revision; a supersession decided against a revision that has since rebound; a receipt naming a revision the graph has moved past. The arranged-layer field is asserted by the suite, not merely documented, so a fixture answered earlier than intended reddens instead of passing.

NOTE ON SCOPE: SCHEDULER_GRAPH_LAYER and WORK_LAYERS appear in this step's description but were already covered in step 2 with the activation-admission group, including the slot-exclusivity race with durable read-back. Not duplicated here.

NEXT: step-4's four scheduler-decision constants (MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS, CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_LAYER, FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_LAYERS, READINESS_LAYERS) and the UNKNOWN-never-zero-never-imputed property, then the five drills. Still uncommitted; both files untracked.

implementationPlan.description:
SCHEDULER DECISION ARMS — MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS, CONVERGENCE_BREAKER_LAYER, FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_LAYERS, READINESS_LAYERS.
HOSTILE INPUT: a usage envelope whose measurement cannot be normalized; a readiness verdict replayed after the graph moved; a fairness decision driven by a forged capacity or in-flight count; a breaker trip presented without the observations that would justify it.
UNKNOWN IS NEVER ZERO AND NEVER IMPUTED — assert it here as a property over the whole group, not per case. An unmeasured usage row, an unresolved readiness verdict and an unobservable capacity each stay UNKNOWN; none is rendered as 0, and none is filled from another attempt's value. This is the single rule these four boundaries exist to hold, and a spreadsheet-shaped scheduler output is exactly where it gets quietly violated.
RACE: a fairness decision racing a convergence breaker trip, and a readiness verdict racing a graph revision. Assert per-side; never two admissions.
COMPLETENESS ACROSS THE SLICE: assert a positive case count per boundary, and assert the union of the three files' swept boundaries equals the roster's 23 scheduler-activation entries in BOTH directions.
WHOLE-SLICE INVARIANT, asserted once over the collected outcomes across all three files rather than per case: no hostile input yields an admitted activation, a consumed grant, an approved expansion, an advanced graph revision, or a truth class above UNKNOWN.
CLEANUP: every filesystem-touching case takes its root from `hostileRoot(label)` or runs inside `withHostileRoot`, with `cleanupHostileRoots()` registered so roots are removed on every exit path including throws and timeouts. Real `SqliteEventStore` for anything that commits, closed in a `finally` — a held handle kills the vitest worker and `fileParallelism: false` means one leak stalls the rest of the lane.
implementationPlan.note:
SCHEDULER DECISION ARMS closed. `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts scheduler-activation-boundaries` => Tests 110 passed (110), EXIT=0 (was 2 failed | 98 passed (100)). Lane `npx tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` => 0 errors repo-wide; my two files had carried ALL SIX of the lane's tsc errors and now carry none.

READINESS_LAYERS — the last uncovered roster entry — is closed, and the compiler had already named the bug: TS2367 "types ... and '"CAPABILITY_AVAILABLE"' have no overlap". `CALLER_FACT_CODES` (readiness-model.ts:191) holds READINESS_CAPABILITY, never CAPABILITY_AVAILABLE, so the old helper overrode NOTHING, every fact stayed CONFIRMED_TRUE and the projection reported dev-ready dispatchable with zero reasons. Measured, then written: capability predicate at UNKNOWN yields {code:READINESS_CAPABILITY, layer:ADMISSION, confidence:UNKNOWN}, arranged ADMISSION. BEFORE = withdrawn predicate; AFTER = projected while dev-ready IS dispatchable, then re-projected after withdrawal, so a memoized/imputed verdict reddens; RACE = UNKNOWN against CONFIRMED_FALSE, neither admitted.

THE TWO-SIDED RULE IS NOW OBSERVABLE, which it was not before: both confidences produce the SAME code and layer, so code+layer alone cannot see a collapse. `projection.withheld` can — UNKNOWN withholds the partition (AVAILABILITY_UNKNOWN, partition null), CONFIRMED_FALSE does not (null, partition present). Asserted as a group property over recorded probes.

A SECOND VACUITY FOUND AND FIXED, in the imputation probe: `unmeasuredUsageAfterSibling` built its prior from `{measurement: null}` (which never normalizes) and then read `prior.value`, a field `MeasurementResult` does not have (TS2339). `undefined` reached production, so NO prior was ever presented and the case tested nothing about imputation. Now a real PROVIDER_REPORTED_COMPLETE observation of run:alpha normalizes first and is passed as `prior`; the unmeasured envelope is still refused BUDGET_OBSERVATION_MALFORMED @ MEASUREMENT. `measurementPrior()` is asserted non-null as the positive control.

Also added: MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS' CONTRACT layer (its list is exactly ["CONTRACT","MEASUREMENT"] and only MEASUREMENT was asserted) — UNKNOWN coverage with quantity 0 refuses BUDGET_MEASUREMENT_COVERAGE_QUANTITY_MISMATCH @ CONTRACT; and a NEGATIVE CONTROL, `honestUnknownFact()`, where UNKNOWN coverage with a null quantity is ACCEPTED and `projectBudgetFact` keeps truthClass UNKNOWN, tier null — without it every refusal is equally explained by a boundary that refuses everything.

BOUND, now explicit rather than the runner default: CASE_BOUND_MS = Math.min(15_000, MAX_BOUND_MS), passed as each `it.each` timeout. DEVIATION disclosed: races drive production's synchronous calls directly rather than through `probeRacing`, because `hostile-harness.ts` is not an owned path and restructuring 25 race entries into thunk pairs would churn a green suite without changing what is bounded. Every race is still asserted per side and order-independent.

Roster re-read from disk at this step: 24 scheduler-activation entries, 89 total, EXPECTED_ROSTER_SIZE 89 — and committed at 5988463, not the uncommitted state the 14:01 governor note described. The both-directions set assertion is green, so the subset equals the roster's 24 exactly.

(1) THE REPLAY-ECHO DRILL: make the activation ledger answer a replay with the caller's own record instead of the durable one; the changed-byte replay case from step 2 MUST redden. THE REPLAY-ECHO TRAP, measured and decisive for `ACTIVATION_LEDGER_LAYER`. `activation-ledger-commit.ts:12-24` states the store's replay identity does NOT cover the events array, which is why that module answers a replay by reading the derived aggregate back rather than echoing the caller. A hostile replay case that presents the SAME record cannot detect an echoing implementation — it compares the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and passes forever. Only a CHANGED-BYTE replay kills it. Drill 1 targets exactly this, and if it stays green the boundary's coverage is vacuous however many cases it has.

ONE-MEMBER VOCABULARY: `SpawnInvocationRefusalCode` (agent-spawn-invocation.ts:19) has exactly ONE member, `"SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE"`, with `SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER = "agent-spawn-invocation"`. A sweep written for a bigger union generates what it finds and passes silently.

LAYERS IN SERIES, three times over on this axis — ingress/slot/budget on one activation; core supersession kernel ahead of the scheduler's disposition; core expansion approval/hold/preparation ahead of the scheduler's binding and evidence. A fixture invalid at the earlier layer is answered there, so the arranged layer must be named per case.

THE AFTER ARM CARRIES THIS AXIS. Almost every boundary here guards "is this decision still bound to the thing it was made about?" — a stale approval, a superseded revision, an expired hold, a moved graph. A BEFORE-only suite would pass against an implementation with no binding recheck at all, which is why step 3 makes the after arm explicit rather than incidental.

BUDGET IS TWO-SIDED: an unmeasured budget and a zero budget are different facts, and `MEASUREMENT_ISSUE_LAYERS` plus `ACTIVATION_BUDGET_LAYER` are where that collapses if it is going to. The scheduler group asserts it as a property rather than per case.

3) A BEFORE-ONLY SUITE passes against an implementation with no binding recheck — and this axis is almost entirely binding rechecks.

4) THREE PLACES WHERE LAYERS SIT IN SERIES. A fixture invalid at the earlier layer is answered there and the assertion silently stops testing its subject. Name the arranged layer per case.
